jobs.description: The Shapiro Center for Creative Writing and Criticism is seeking an Assistant Professor of the Practice or Associate Professor of the Practice in Journalism, beginning July 1, 2027. jobs.description: Wesleyan University's Department of Art and Art History invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Art History beginning July 1, 2027. We seek an historian of pre-modern Islamic Art, working on periods before 1800. We welcome specialists in any subfield or geographic region, pursuing any methodological approach/es; special consideration will be given to scholars of South, Central, and/or West Asian art. Candidates from the fields of art and architectural history and archaeology are welcome to apply. Wesleyan is a highly selective liberal arts college; the teaching load is 2/2 on campus. Additional duties include advising and mentoring students, carrying out a program of research, and participating in faculty governance at the departmental and university level. Wesleyan values both scholarship and teaching very highly, has a strong, widely varied undergraduate student body, and offers a generous sabbatical program and competitive salaries and benefits. Successful candidates will join a distinguished Art History Program which shares the university’s commitment to teaching and research. It is expected that candidates will maintain a robust scholarly practice, as a strong publishing record will be expected for promotion. Minimum Qualifications Ph.D. in Art History or a related field in hand by the time of appointment to be hired as an Assistant Professor; a successful candidate may be hired as an Instructor if the candidate does not have a Ph.D. in hand at the time of appointment, but will complete the Ph.D. in Art History or a related field within one year of hire. Special Instructions to Applicants A complete application includes the following materials, uploaded in the order shown, with each numbered item combined into a single document: (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) statement of current research; (4) writing sample (such as a dissertation chapter or published article); and (5) documentation of teaching interests and/or experience, including teaching statement and course syllabi as well as student evaluations if available. In the cover letter, applicants should describe how they will embrace the college’s commitment to fostering an inclusive community. You will also be asked to provide the email addresses of three referees from whom we will obtain confidential letters of recommendation. Applications completed by December 1, 2026 will receive full consideration. jobs.description: Job Description: The School of Engineering and Computing at Fairfield University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the assistant professor rank in the Michael Zabinski Department of Mechanical Engineering. The start date for this position is September 1st, 2027, pending budget approval. Candidates in all areas of Mechanical Engineering or closely related fields are encouraged to apply. Position Description : This position requires an ability to perform teaching, scholarship, and service responsibilities. The successful candidate will be required to: (1) develop and teach undergraduate and graduate courses (lecture and laboratory) in mechanical engineering. (2) supervise Master theses, undergraduate research, capstone projects, and senior design projects; (3) pursue scholarly activities (including externally-funded research and peer-reviewed publications); (4) engage in academic advising and mentoring; and (5) assist in program assessment, execution of the department’s continuous improvement plan, and documentation in support of ABET accreditation. The position is an academic (9-month), tenure-track appointment, and the salaries are competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. The School of Engineering and Computing is organized into the Michael Zabinski Department of Mechanical Engineering, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, and the Department of Electrical, Mechatronics, and Biomedical Engineering. The Mechanical Engineering program is ABET accredited and offers Bachelor of Science and Master of Science degrees. In addition, students have an option to obtain a Concentration in either Automation, Robotics, and Manufacturing or Aerospace Engineering. The department is equipped with state-of-the-art laboratories such as Material Characterization Lab, Automation, Robotics and Manufacturing (A.R.M.) Lab, Mechanical Engineering Lab, and the High-Speed Fluids Research Lab. It also houses the Brinkman Manufacturing Laboratory and the Innovation Annex in support of teaching and research and boasts the highest undergraduate enrollment within the School of Engineering. Required Qualifications : A Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering or closely related discipline. Effective verbal and written communication skills. Ability to effectively teach both undergraduate and graduate courses, including hands-on labs. Demonstrated potential to engage in funded research in a relevant field, along with a demonstrable publication record. Preferred Qualifications : Candidates with expertise in experimental and applied areas of Mechanical Engineering are encouraged to apply. Computational expertise is considered a favorable additional qualification when complemented by hands-on, applied research and teaching experience. Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, solid mechanics/structures, thermal-fluid sciences, energy, aerospace, and other emerging areas of Mechanical Engineering. Screening of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Full consideration will be given to candidates who apply by November 1st, 2026. The preferred starting date is September 1st, 2027. Please combine and upload the following materials in a single PDF document . A complete application will consist of: (1) a cover letter addressing the qualifications (one-page), (2) a statement of teaching interests and research plan (two pages), (3) a curriculum vitae, and (4) the names and contact information of three professional references (references will not be contacted without prior knowledge and approval of candidates). Applicants are encouraged to submit a project portfolio (three to five pages with annotated photographs or a link to a website repository) that illustrates hands-on, project-based contributions. Only complete electronic applications will be considered. Inquiries about the position should be addressed to the Chair of the Search Committee, Dr. David Shekhtman

This position is part of a multi-departmental cluster hire in quantum science—the first phase of a "Quantum Futures Cluster"— supporting UConn’s leadership in the NSF Quantum Technologies Engine in Connecticut (QuantumCT Engine). The hire is central to a major, long-term strategic investment to establish Connecticut as a national leader in quantum technology. To strengthen the research and educational missions identified in the strategic plans of the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and the University, we seek a mathematician or statistician with expertise in quantum algorithms, quantum information science, optimization, and post-quantum cryptography to advance the goals of the QuantumCT Engine and create natural synergies with AI for ImpaCT, a university-wide initiative to drive AI innovations across Connecticut. We invite applications from candidates across a broad spectrum of quantum-related research in Mathematics or Statistics. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of next-generation quantum methodologies and help shape the future of mathematics and statistics in the quantum era. The QuantumCT Engine aims to advance American quantum innovation and secure the domestic quantum supply chain by accelerating the commercialization of quantum technologies for national defense, biotechnology and financial services.
